feedback_request.compare_against: Iteration 7 / 9 (wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.6, y = 0.08), score 75.9247. Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.10, y = 0.07) for the over-response effect.

intent: Keep the iteration 9 (= iteration 7) design and change one thing: wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.11 m. Integrator: keep kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, last_direction line-loss recovery, and the 25-times-x sensor weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2) with no gain change. Expected result: oval progress at or above 0.2725, s-bend progress near 0.157 with steering oscillation at or below 0.15, and slalom progress near 0.109 with at most 1.0 line loss per run. Decision rule for iteration 11: if s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.15 or slalom line losses exceed 1.0, restore wheel_track 0.12 (the iteration 7 design) for the final race. If oval progress and score both exceed 75.92 with the other limits held, keep wheel_track 0.11.
learning: Evidence: the best design (iteration 7, reproduced in iteration 9) has oval progress 0.2725 with max_error at the 0.06 floor, s-bend progress 0.1573 with oscillation 0.135, and slalom progress 0.1094 with 1.0 line loss per run. Iteration 8 (mass 0.5) lost the oval gain, so the oval is sensitive to mass. Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.10, y = 0.07) raised s-bend oscillation to 0.164, but oval progress did not move with track width at that lead. Hypothesis A: a modest narrowing to 0.11 gives enough extra turn authority to lift the oval max_error below the floor while keeping s-bend oscillation under 0.15. Hypothesis B: the narrower track pushes the s-bend and slalom into over-response, so the iteration 7 track width is the best trade-off.
rationale: Iteration 9 reproduced iteration 7 exactly (score 75.9247, oval progress 0.2725, s-bend 0.1573, slalom 1.0 line loss per run). The simulator is deterministic per seed and track, so the best design is stable and the result is not seed noise. The one open question is whether turn authority can be raised without losing the oval gain. Iteration 4 showed that narrowing the track from 0.12 to 0.10 at y = 0.07 raised s-bend oscillation to 0.164 and slalom line losses to 0.95, but that test used a large step at a different lead. Iteration 7's s-bend oscillation at y = 0.08 is 0.135, which leaves room for a smaller step. I therefore test wheel_track 0.11, the single change that Entity R1 identified as the next test if the iteration 7 result reproduces. Mass 0.6, lead y = 0.08, 16 mm sensors, the 0.16 m x 0.14 m body, wheel radius 0.03 and the 25-per-metre weights (controller side) are all unchanged. Expected result: oval progress near or above 0.27, s-bend steering oscillation at or below about 0.15, and slalom line losses at or below 1.0. Risk: the narrower track raises turn rate by about 9 percent for the same controller output, so the s-bend and slalom may over-respond as they did at 0.10. If that happens, iteration 11 should restore wheel_track 0.12 and the iteration 7 design, which is the known best. Iteration 11 is the last iteration, so I will not test another geometry lever after this one unless this result is clearly better.
